name_translation: The Yoga of the Imperishable Absolute

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
किं तद्ब्रह्म किमध्यात्मं किं कर्म पुरुषोत्तम |
अधिभूतं च किं प्रोक्तमधिदैवं किमुच्यते || १ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
किं तद्ब्रह्म किमध्यात्मं किं कर्म पुरुषोत्तम |
अधिभूतं च किं प्रोक्तमधिदैवं किमुच्यते || १ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
kiṃ tadbrahma kimadhyātmaṃ kiṃ karma puruṣottama |
adhibhūtaṃ ca kiṃ proktamadhidaivaṃ kimucyate || 1 ||
verses.word_meanings: arjunaḥ uvāca—Arjuna said; kim—what; tat—that; brahma—Brahman (the Absolute Reality); kim—what; adhyātmam—Adhyatma (the inner Self); kim—what; karma—Karma (action); puruṣottama—O Supreme Person; adhibhūtam—Adhibhuta (the physical/material sphere); ca—and; kim—what; proktam—is called; adhidaivam—Adhidaiva (the celestial sphere); kim—what; ucyate—is said to be.
verses.translation: Arjuna said: O Supreme Person (Purushottama), what is that Brahman? What is Adhyatma (the inner Self)? What is Karma (action)? What is called Adhibhuta (the material sphere)? And what is spoken of as Adhidaiva (the celestial sphere)?
verses.meaning: Arjuna opens the eighth chapter by posing seven profound metaphysical inquiries prompted by Sri Krishna's closing statements in Chapter 7. He seeks precise definitions for the core ontological principles of existence: the Absolute Reality (Brahman), the indwelling Self (Adhyatma), the nature of creative cosmic action (Karma), the mutable physical cosmos (Adhibhuta), and the cosmic presiding deities (Adhidaiva).
verses.purport: Arjuna opens the eighth chapter by posing seven profound metaphysical inquiries prompted by Sri Krishna's closing statements in Chapter 7. verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अधियज्ञः कथं कोऽत्र देहेऽस्मिन्मधुसूदन |
प्रयाणकाले च कथं ज्ञेयोऽसि नियतात्मभिः || २ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अधियज्ञः कथं कोऽत्र देहेऽस्मिन्मधुसूदन |
प्रयाणकाले च कथं ज्ञेयोऽसि नियतात्मभिः || २ ||
verses.transliteration:
adhiyajñaḥ kathaṃ ko'tra dehe'sminmadhusūdana |
prayāṇakāle ca kathaṃ jñeyo'si niyatātmabhiḥ || 2 ||
verses.word_meanings: adhiyajñaḥ—the Lord of sacrifice (Adhiyajna); katham—how; kaḥ—who; atra—here; dehe—in the body; asmin—in this; madhusūdana—O slayer of Madhu (Sri Krishna); prayāṇa-kāle—at the time of departure (death); ca—and; katham—how; jñeyaḥ asi—are You to be known; niyata-ātmabhiḥ—by the self-controlled practitioners.
verses.translation: Who is Adhiyajna (the Lord of Sacrifice), and how does He dwell in this body, O Madhusudana? And how can You be known at the critical moment of death by those of self-disciplined minds?
verses.meaning: Arjuna completes his inquiry with two vital questions: the identity of Adhiyajna (the cosmic and bodily Lord of Sacrifice) and the ultimate spiritual secret of how a disciplined seeker can maintain divine consciousness and remember the Supreme Lord at the moment of departing this mortal body (Prayanakale).
verses.purport: Arjuna completes his inquiry with two vital questions: the identity of Adhiyajna (the cosmic and bodily Lord of Sacrifice) and the ultimate spiritual secret of how a disciplined seeker can maintain divine consciousness and remember the Supreme Lord at the moment of departing this mortal body (Prayanakale).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अक्षरं ब्रह्म परमं स्वभावोऽध्यात्ममुच्यते |
भूतभावोद्भवकरो विसर्गः कर्मसञ्ज्ञितः || ३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अक्षरं ब्रह्म परमं स्वभावोऽध्यात्ममुच्यते |
भूतभावोद्भवकरो विसर्गः कर्मसञ्ज्ञितः || ३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
akṣaraṃ brahma paramaṃ svabhāvo'dhyātmamucyate |
bhūtabhāvodbhavakaro visargaḥ karmasañjñitaḥ || 3 ||
verses.word_meanings: śrī-bhagavān uvāca—the Supreme Lord said; akṣaram—imperishable; brahma—the Absolute Reality; paramam—supreme; svabhāvaḥ—essential nature (the indwelling spirit); adhyātmam—Adhyatma (the inner Self); ucyate—is called; bhūta-bhāva-udbhava-karaḥ—that which causes the birth and manifestation of living beings; visargaḥ—the creative sacrificial emission; karma-sañjñitaḥ—is designated as Karma (action).
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: The Supreme Imperishable Reality is Brahman. Its essential nature dwelling within the individual is called Adhyatma. The creative sacrificial offering that brings forth the existence and bodies of living beings is termed Karma (action).
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna systematically answers Arjuna's first three questions. Brahman is the indestructible, transcendent, absolute Consciousness (Akshara Parama). Adhyatma is the subjective spiritual essence (the indwelling Jivatman) which manifests through each individual. Karma refers to the cosmic sacrificial discharge (Visarga) of creative energy that generates, sustains, and evolves all material bodies and manifestations.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अधिभूतं क्षरो भावः पुरुषश्चाधिदैवतम् |
अधियज्ञोऽहमेवात्र देहे देहभृतां वर || ४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अधिभूतं क्षरो भावः पुरुषश्चाधिदैवतम् |
अधियज्ञोऽहमेवात्र देहे देहभृतां वर || ४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
adhibhūtaṃ kṣaro bhāvaḥ puruṣaścādhidaivatam |
adhiyajño'hamevātra dehe dehabhṛtāṃ vara || 4 ||
verses.word_meanings: adhibhūtam—the material realm; kṣaraḥ bhāvaḥ—perishable nature; puruṣaḥ—the cosmic person (Hiranyagarbha); ca—and; adhidaivatam—the presiding celestial realm; adhiyajñaḥ—the Lord of sacrifice; aham eva—I alone; atra—here; dehe—in the body; deha-bhṛtām vara—O best of the embodied (Arjuna).
verses.translation: The perishable material creation is called Adhibhuta. The cosmic universal person (Hiranyagarbha) is called Adhidaiva. And I alone am Adhiyajna (the Supreme Lord of Sacrifice) indwelling here within this body, O best of embodied beings.
verses.meaning: The Lord defines the remaining principles. Adhibhuta comprises all perishable, transient physical nature (Kshara Bhava). Adhidaiva is the Purusha, the universal macrocosmic consciousness and presiding spirit behind the celestial devas. Adhiyajna is Sri Krishna Himself as the Paramatman (Supersoul) dwelling directly in the heart of every embodied living entity, receiving every breath, act, and sacrifice.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अन्तकाले च मामेव स्मरन्मुक्त्वा कलेवरम् |
यः प्रयाति स मद्भावं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः || ५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अन्तकाले च मामेव स्मरन्मुक्त्वा कलेवरम् |
यः प्रयाति स मद्भावं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः || ५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
antakāle ca māmeva smaranmuktvā kalevaram |
yaḥ prayāti sa madbhāvaṃ yāti nāstyatra saṃśayaḥ || 5 ||
verses.word_meanings: anta-kāle—at the final hour (moment of death); ca—and; mām eva—Me alone; smaran—remembering; muktvā—abandoning, leaving; kalevaram—the physical body; yaḥ—whoever; prayāti—departs; saḥ—he; mad-bhāvam—My divine nature; yāti—attains; na asti—there is not; atra—in this; saṃśayaḥ—doubt.
verses.translation: And whoever, at the time of death, leaves the body remembering Me alone, attains My divine state of being; of this there is no doubt.
verses.meaning: This is one of the most celebrated and reassuring verses in the Gita. Sri Krishna reveals the definitive law of consciousness at the moment of physical death (Antakale). If the departing soul's awareness is wholly immersed in remembrance of the Supreme Lord, it is immediately freed from the wheel of samsara and attains Mad-bhavam—eternal union with Krishna's divine nature.
verses.purport: This is one of the most celebrated and reassuring verses in the Gita. Sri Krishna reveals the definitive law of consciousness at the moment of physical death (Antakale). verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम् |
तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः || ६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम् |
तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः || ६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaranbhāvaṃ tyajatyante kalevaram |
taṃ tamevaiti kaunteya sadā tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ || 6 ||
verses.word_meanings: yam yam—whatever; vā api—even; smaran—remembering; bhāvam—state of being; tyajati—gives up; ante—at the end; kalevaram—the body; tam tam eva—to that very state; eti—goes; kaunteya—O son of Kunti; sadā—always; tat-bhāva-bhāvitaḥ—absorbed in that contemplation.
verses.translation: Whatever state of being one remembers when abandoning the body at the end, that state alone does one attain, O son of Kunti, having been constantly absorbed in the contemplation thereof.
verses.meaning: The Lord explains the fundamental psychological and spiritual mechanics of reincarnation. The final thought at death is not an accidental occurrence, but the distilled essence of one's lifelong preoccupations, desires, and habits of mind (Sada tad-bhava-bhavitah). Hence, spiritual discipline during lifetime is essential so that divine contemplation arises naturally at the moment of departure.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च |
मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयम् || ७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च |
मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयम् || ७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
tasmātsarveṣu kāleṣu māmanusmara yudhya ca |
mayyarpitamanobuddhirmāmevaiṣyasyasaṃśayam || 7 ||
verses.word_meanings: tasmāt—therefore; sarveṣu kāleṣu—at all times; mām—Me; anusmara—remember; yudhya ca—and fight; mayi—in Me; arpita-manaḥ-buddhiḥ—having surrendered mind and intellect; mām eva—to Me alone; eṣyasi—you shall come; asaṃśayam—without any doubt.
verses.translation: Therefore, at all times remember Me and fight. With your mind and intellect surrender-focused on Me, you shall without doubt attain Me alone.
verses.meaning: A crowning injunction of practical spiritual living: 'Mamanusmara yudhya cha' (Remember Me and fight). Krishna does not advocate abandoning duty for seclusion; rather, He teaches the integration of active duty in the world with uninterrupted inner remembrance of God. By dedicating both emotional mind (Manas) and analytical intellect (Buddhi) to the Divine, every action becomes a sacred offering leading to liberation.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अभ्यासयोगयुक्तेन चेतसा नान्यगामिना |
परमं पुरुषं दिव्यं याति पार्थानुचिन्तयन् || ८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अभ्यासयोगयुक्तेन चेतसा नान्यगामिना |
परमं पुरुषं दिव्यं याति पार्थानुचिन्तयन् || ८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
abhyāsayogayuktena cetasā nānyagāminā |
paramaṃ puruṣaṃ divyaṃ yāti pārthānucintayan || 8 ||
verses.word_meanings: abhyāsa-yoga-yuktena—by practice of yoga of meditation; cetasā—with the mind; na anya-gāminā—not wandering elsewhere; paramam—the Supreme; puruṣam—Person; divyam—divine, transcendental; yāti—attains; pārtha—O son of Pritha (Arjuna); anucintayan—constantly meditating upon.
verses.translation: Endowed with the practice of steady yogic meditation, with a mind that does not wander after anything else, constantly meditating on the Supreme Divine Person, O Partha, one attains Him.
verses.meaning: Constant meditation (Abhyasa-yoga) trains the restless mind to remain anchored in the Supreme Divine Person (Parama Purusha Divya). Through repeated, disciplined focus that rejects worldly distractions (nanya-gamina), the consciousness naturally gravitates toward God at the moment of death.
verses.purport: Constant meditation (Abhyasa-yoga) trains the restless mind to remain anchored in the Supreme Divine Person (Parama Purusha Divya). verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
कविं पुराणमनुशासितार-
मणोरणीयांसमनुस्मरेद्यः |
सर्वस्य धातारमचिन्त्यरूप-
मादित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात् || ९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
कविं पुराणमनुशासितार-
मणोरणीयांसमनुस्मरेद्यः |
सर्वस्य धातारमचिन्त्यरूप-
मादित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात् || ९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
kaviṃ purāṇamanuśāsitāra-
maṇoraṇīyāṃsamanusmaredyaḥ |
sarvasya dhātāramacintyarūpa-
mādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt || 9 ||
verses.word_meanings: kavim—the all-knowing seer (omniscient); purāṇam—the primeval/ancient; anuśāsitāram—the supreme ruler and governor; aṇoḥ aṇīyāṃsam—subtler than the subtlest atom; anusmaret yaḥ—whoever remembers; sarvasya dhātāram—the sustainer of all; acintya-rūpam—of inconceivable form; āditya-varṇam—radiant like the sun; tamasaḥ parastāt—transcending the darkness of ignorance.
verses.translation: Whoever constantly meditates upon the Omniscient Seer (Kavi), the Ancient of Days (Purana), the Supreme Governor and Lawgiver of all, subtler than the subtlest atom, the Sustainer of all existence, whose divine form is beyond all human comprehension, radiant like the sun beyond the darkness of ignorance...
verses.meaning: Krishna describes the sublime attributes of the Supreme Being to guide the seeker's meditation: He is Kavi (the all-knowing seer of past, present, and future), Purana (beginningless and eternal), Anushasitara (the supreme moral and cosmic ruler), Anoraniyan (subtler than subatomic particles, permeating everything), Sarvasya Dhata (the dispenser of cosmic fruit and sustainer of life), Achintyarupa (beyond finite mental imagination), and Adityavarna (effulgent like the sun, transcending all darkness).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
प्रयाणकाले मनसाऽचलेन
भक्त्या युक्तो योगबलेन चैव |
भ्रुवोर्मध्ये प्राणमावेश्य सम्यक्
स तं परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम् || १० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
प्रयाणकाले मनसाऽचलेन
भक्त्या युक्तो योगबलेन चैव |
भ्रुवोर्मध्ये प्राणमावेश्य सम्यक्
स तं परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम् || १० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
prayāṇakāle manasā'calena
bhaktyā yukto yogabalena caiva |
bhruvormadhye prāṇamāveśya samyak
sa taṃ paraṃ puruṣamupaiti divyam || 10 ||
verses.word_meanings: prayāṇa-kāle—at the time of departure; manasā acalena—with an unwavering mind; bhaktyā yuktaḥ—endowed with devotion; yoga-balena ca eva—and by the power of yoga; bhruvoḥ madhye—between the eyebrows (Ajna Chakra); prāṇam—the vital life force; āveśya samyak—having fully fixed/focused; saḥ—he; tam—that; param puruṣam—Supreme Person; upaiti—attains; divyam—transcendental, divine.
verses.translation: At the time of departure, with an unmoving mind, endowed with devotion and the power of yoga, having correctly concentrated the vital life-force (Prana) between the eyebrows (Ajna Chakra), he attains that Supreme Divine Person.
verses.meaning: Here Sri Krishna synthesizes Bhakti (heartfelt devotion) with Raja Yoga (mastery of life-energy). At the moment of physical death, the accomplished yogi gathers all sensory currents and anchors the vital breath (Prana) in the Ajna Chakra between the eyebrows, passing beyond worldly relativity into eternal union with the Parama Purusha.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यदक्षरं वेदविदो वदन्ति
विशन्ति यद्यतयो वीतरागाः |
यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्ति
तत्ते पदं सङ्ग्रहेण प्रवक्ष्ये || ११ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यदक्षरं वेदविदो वदन्ति
विशन्ति यद्यतयो वीतरागाः |
यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्ति
तत्ते पदं सङ्ग्रहेण प्रवक्ष्ये || ११ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yadakṣaraṃ vedavido vadanti
viśanti yadyatayo vītarāgāḥ |
yadicchanto brahmacaryaṃ caranti
tatte padaṃ saṅgraheṇa pravakṣye || 11 ||
verses.word_meanings: yat—which; akṣaram—imperishable; veda-vidaḥ—knowers of the Vedas; vadanti—declare; viśanti—enter; yat—which; yatayaḥ—renunciants/ascetics; vīta-rāgāḥ—freed from passion and attachment; yat—which; icchantaḥ—desiring; brahmacaryam—the vow of celibacy/spiritual discipline; caranti—practice; tat te padam—that state to you; saṅgraheṇa—in brief; pravakṣye—I shall declare.
verses.translation: That which the knowers of the Vedas declare as the Imperishable (Akshara), into which the ascetics freed from attachment enter, and desiring which they practice the vow of celibate spiritual discipline (Brahmacharya)—that supreme state I shall briefly explain to you.
verses.meaning: Echoing the renowned verse from the Katha Upanishad (1.2.15), Krishna introduces the classical Vedic path of meditation on the unmanifest Absolute, pursued by dispassionate ascetics (Yatis) dedicated to self-restraint and celibacy.
verses.purport: Echoing the renowned verse from the Katha Upanishad (1.2.15), Krishna introduces the classical Vedic path of meditation on the unmanifest Absolute, pursued by dispassionate ascetics (Yatis) dedicated to self-restraint and celibacy.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च |
मूर्ध्न्याधायात्मनः प्राणमास्थितो योगधारणाम् || १२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च |
मूर्ध्न्याधायात्मनः प्राणमास्थितो योगधारणाम् || १२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
sarvadvārāṇi saṃyamya mano hṛdi nirudhya ca |
mūrdhnyādhāyātmanaḥ prāṇamāsthito yogadhāraṇām || 12 ||
verses.word_meanings: sarva-dvārāṇi—all the sensory doors/gates; saṃyamya—controlling, closing; manaḥ—the mind; hṛdi—in the heart; nirudhya—confining; ca—and; mūrdhni—in the crown of the head (Sahasrara); ādhāya—fixing; ātmanaḥ prāṇam—one's vital life-force; āsthitaḥ—established; yoga-dhāraṇām—in yogic concentration.
verses.translation: Closing all the gates of the senses, confining the mind within the cave of the heart, and fixing the vital life-breath in the crown of the head (Sahasrara), established in firm yogic concentration...
verses.meaning: The inner method of departure through yogic concentration (Yoga-dharana): The seeker withdraws perception from the nine somatic gates (eyes, ears, nostrils, mouth, etc.), collects mental focus in the heart center, and directs the subtle Prana upward through the Sushumna nadi to the crown of the head.
verses.purport: The inner method of departure through yogic concentration (Yoga-dharana): The seeker withdraws perception from the nine somatic gates (eyes, ears, nostrils, mouth, etc.), collects mental focus in the heart center, and directs the subtle Prana upward through the Sushumna nadi to the crown of the head.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन् |
यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम् || १३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन् |
यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम् || १३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
omityekākṣaraṃ brahma vyāharanmāmanusmaran |
yaḥ prayāti tyajandehaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim || 13 ||
verses.word_meanings: om—the sacred syllable OM; iti—thus; eka-akṣaram—single syllable; brahma—the Absolute; vyāharan—uttering/chanting; mām—Me; anusmaran—remembering; yaḥ—whoever; prayāti—departs; tyajan deham—quitting the body; saḥ—he; yāti—attains; paramām gatim—the supreme destination.
verses.translation: Uttering the single sacred syllable OM, which is Brahman, and constantly remembering Me, whoever departs casting off the body attains the Supreme Destination.
verses.meaning: Pranava OM is the primordial sonic vibration of the Absolute (Shabda Brahman). Meditating upon its vibration while holding Sri Krishna in the heart at the time of leaving the body grants immediate entry into the highest spiritual dimension (Paramam Gatim) from which there is no rebirth.
verses.purport: Pranava OM is the primordial sonic vibration of the Absolute (Shabda Brahman). Meditating upon its vibration while holding Sri Krishna in the heart at the time of leaving the body grants immediate entry into the highest spiritual dimension (Paramam Gatim) from which there is no rebirth.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः |
तस्याहं सुलभः पार्थ नित्ययुक्तस्य योगिनः || १४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः |
तस्याहं सुलभः पार्थ नित्ययुक्तस्य योगिनः || १४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ananyacetāḥ satataṃ yo māṃ smarati nityaśaḥ |
tasyāhaṃ sulabhaḥ pārtha nityayuktasya yoginaḥ || 14 ||
verses.word_meanings: ananya-cetāḥ—with single-minded focus; satatam—always; yaḥ—whoever; mām—Me; smarati—remembers; nityaśaḥ—regularly/daily; tasya—for him; aham—I am; su-labhaḥ—easily attainable; pārtha—O son of Pritha; nitya-yuktasya—ever-absorbed; yoginaḥ—for the yogi.
verses.translation: For the yogi who constantly and single-mindedly remembers Me with unwavering devotion, O Partha, I am easily attained, because of their constant absorption in Me.
verses.meaning: While the path of Ashtanga and Kundalini yoga requires rigorous technical mastery, Krishna emphasizes that pure love and undivided absorption (Ananya-chetah) make God-realization effortlessly accessible (Sulabha). The Lord is ever near to those whose hearts constantly beat for Him.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मामुपेत्य पुनर्जन्म दुःखालयमशाश्वतम् |
नाप्नुवन्ति महात्मानः संसिद्धिं परमां गताः || १५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मामुपेत्य पुनर्जन्म दुःखालयमशाश्वतम् |
नाप्नुवन्ति महात्मानः संसिद्धिं परमां गताः || १५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
māmupetya punarjanma duḥkhālayamaśāśvatam |
nāpnuvanti mahātmānaḥ saṃsiddhiṃ paramāṃ gatāḥ || 15 ||
verses.word_meanings: mām upetya—having reached Me; punaḥ janma—rebirth; duḥkha-ālayam—abode of sorrows; aśāśvatam—impermanent, transient; na āpnuvanti—do not attain; mahātmānaḥ—great souls; saṃsiddhim paramām—the highest perfection; gatāḥ—having reached.
verses.translation: Having attained Me, these great souls (Mahatmas) never again take rebirth in this transient world which is an abode of sorrows; they have achieved the highest spiritual perfection.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna characterizes the mortal realm as 'Dukhalayam' (an abode of miseries) and 'Ashashvatam' (fleeting, ephemeral). Great enlightened souls who reach Krishna's transcendental abode transcend mortality, disease, and grief forever.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna characterizes the mortal realm as 'Dukhalayam' (an abode of miseries) and 'Ashashvatam' (fleeting, ephemeral). Great enlightened souls who reach Krishna's transcendental abode transcend mortality, disease, and grief forever.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
आब्रह्मभुवनाल्लोकाः पुनरावर्तिनोऽर्जुन |
मामुपेत्य तु कौन्तेय पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते || १६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
आब्रह्मभुवनाल्लोकाः पुनरावर्तिनोऽर्जुन |
मामुपेत्य तु कौन्तेय पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते || १६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ābrahmabhuvanāllokāḥ punarāvartino'rjuna |
māmupetya tu kaunteya punarjanma na vidyate || 16 ||
verses.word_meanings: ā-brahma-bhuvanāt—up to the realm of Brahma; lokāḥ—all planetary systems/worlds; punaḥ āvartinaḥ—subject to return/rebirth; arjuna—O Arjuna; mām upetya—having attained Me; tu—but; kaunteya—O son of Kunti; punaḥ janma—rebirth; na vidyate—does not exist.
verses.translation: All the worlds up to the realm of Brahma (Brahmaloka) are subject to return, O Arjuna; but having reached Me, O son of Kunti, there is no rebirth.
verses.meaning: Even the highest celestial heavens, including the majestic abode of creator Brahma, are temporal spheres bounded by cosmic time and subject to dissolution (Pralaya). Residence in these realms ends when one's pious karma is exhausted. Only Krishna's supreme spiritual domain lies beyond time and provides eternal liberation.

Residence in these realms ends when one's pious karma is exhausted. Only Krishna's supreme spiritual domain lies beyond time and provides eternal liberation.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तमहर्यद्ब्रह्मणो विदुः |
रात्रिं युगसहस्रान्तां तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः || १७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तमहर्यद्ब्रह्मणो विदुः |
रात्रिं युगसहस्रान्तां तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः || १७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
sahasrayugaparyantamaharyadbrahmaṇo viduḥ |
rātriṃ yugasahasrāntāṃ te'horātravido janāḥ || 17 ||
verses.word_meanings: sahasra-yuga-paryantam—extending for a thousand cosmic ages (yugas); ahaḥ—day; yat—which; brahmaṇaḥ—of Brahma (the creator); viduḥ—they know; rātrim—night; yuga-sahasra-antām—ending after a thousand yugas; te—they; ahaḥ-rātra-vidaḥ—knowers of day and night; janāḥ—people.
verses.translation: Those who know that the cosmic day of Brahma extends for a thousand Mahayugas (4.32 billion human years), and that his night also spans a thousand Mahayugas, are truly knowers of the day and night of cosmic time.
verses.meaning: A breathtaking exposition of Vedic cosmic time: A single daytime period of Brahma (a Kalpa) lasts 1,000 cycles of four yugas (Satya, Treta, Dvapara, Kali), totaling 4.32 billion solar years, followed by an equally long cosmic night of rest and dissolution. Knowers of this cycle understand the microscopic insignificance of mortal life compared to cosmic eternity.

Knowers of this cycle understand the microscopic insignificance of mortal life compared to cosmic eternity.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अव्यक्ताद्व्यक्तयः सर्वाः प्रभवन्त्यहरागमे |
रात्र्यागमे प्रलीयन्ते तत्रैवाव्यक्तसञ्ज्ञके || १८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अव्यक्ताद्व्यक्तयः सर्वाः प्रभवन्त्यहरागमे |
रात्र्यागमे प्रलीयन्ते तत्रैवाव्यक्तसञ्ज्ञके || १८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
avyaktādvyaktayaḥ sarvāḥ prabhavantyaharāgame |
rātryāgame pralīyante tatraivāvyaktasañjñake || 18 ||
verses.word_meanings: avyaktāt—from the unmanifest; vyaktayaḥ sarvāḥ—all manifest beings and forms; prabhavanti—emanate/emerge; ahara-āgame—at the dawn of day; rātri-āgame—at the onset of night; pralīyante—they dissolve; tatra eva—in that very; avyakta-sañjñake—called the unmanifest.
verses.translation: At the arrival of Brahma's day, all manifest entities emerge from the unmanifest cosmic nature; and at the arrival of Brahma's night, they dissolve back into that very unmanifest state.
verses.meaning: The rhythm of cosmic creation (Srishti) and cosmic dissolution (Pralaya). During Brahma's active day, the seeds of unmanifest karma sprout into diverse planetary systems and physical forms; when Brahma sleeps, all created forms withdraw and rest in dormant potentiality within Prakriti.
verses.purport: The rhythm of cosmic creation (Srishti) and cosmic dissolution (Pralaya). During Brahma's active day, the seeds of unmanifest karma sprout into diverse planetary systems and physical forms; when Brahma sleeps, all created forms withdraw and rest in dormant potentiality within Prakriti.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते |
रात्र्यागमेऽवशः पार्थ प्रभवत्यहरागमे || १९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते |
रात्र्यागमेऽवशः पार्थ प्रभवत्यहरागमे || १९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
bhūtagrāmaḥ sa evāyaṃ bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyate |
rātryāgame'vaśaḥ pārtha prabhavatyaharāgame || 19 ||
verses.word_meanings: bhūta-grāmaḥ—multitude of living beings; saḥ eva ayam—this very same; bhūtvā bhūtvā—having repeatedly come into being; pralīyate—dissolves; rātri-āgame—at the coming of night; avaśaḥ—helplessly; pārtha—O son of Pritha; prabhavati—manifests; ahara-āgame—at the coming of day.
verses.translation: This very multitude of living beings, coming into being again and again, dissolves helplessly at the arrival of night, O Partha, and springs into manifestation once more at the arrival of day.
verses.meaning: Living beings bound by material desires and past karmas (Bhuta-gramah) are swept cyclically through infinite births and dissolutions without personal autonomy (Avashah), being repeatedly projected at creation and swallowed at dissolution until they achieve self-realization.
verses.purport: Living beings bound by material desires and past karmas (Bhuta-gramah) are swept cyclically through infinite births and dissolutions without personal autonomy (Avashah), being repeatedly projected at creation and swallowed at dissolution until they achieve self-realization.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
परस्तस्मात्तु भावोऽन्योऽव्यक्तोऽव्यक्तात्सनातनः |
यः स सर्वेषु भूतेषु नश्यत्सु न विनश्यति || २० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
परस्तस्मात्तु भावोऽन्योऽव्यक्तोऽव्यक्तात्सनातनः |
यः स सर्वेषु भूतेषु नश्यत्सु न विनश्यति || २० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
parastasmāttu bhāvo'nyo'vyakto'vyaktātsanātanaḥ |
yaḥ sa sarveṣu bhūteṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati || 20 ||
verses.word_meanings: paraḥ—transcendental, beyond; tasmāt—than that; tu—but; bhāvaḥ anyaḥ—another state/reality; avyaktaḥ—unmanifest; avyaktāt—than the unmanifest (material energy); sanātanaḥ—eternal, beginningless; yaḥ saḥ—which; sarveṣu bhūteṣu—when all beings; naśyatsu—are destroyed; na vinaśyati—is never destroyed.
verses.translation: Yet beyond this unmanifest material nature, there exists another unmanifest, eternal spiritual reality, which does not perish even when all living entities are annihilated.
verses.meaning: Beyond both the manifest universe (Vyakta) and the unmanifest material energy (Avyakta Prakriti) lies the transcendental spiritual realm (Sanatana Avyakta). This is the eternal, immutable nature of the Supreme Lord which remains completely untouched and radiant even when the entire cosmos dissolves.
verses.purport: Beyond both the manifest universe (Vyakta) and the unmanifest material energy (Avyakta Prakriti) lies the transcendental spiritual realm (Sanatana Avyakta). This is the eternal, immutable nature of the Supreme Lord which remains completely untouched and radiant even when the entire cosmos dissolves.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अव्यक्तोऽक्षर इत्युक्तस्तमाहुः परमां गतिम् |
यं प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम || २१ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अव्यक्तोऽक्षर इत्युक्तस्तमाहुः परमां गतिम् |
यं प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम || २१ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
avyakto'kṣara ityuktastamāhuḥ paramāṃ gatim |
yaṃ prāpya na nivartante taddhāma paramaṃ mama || 21 ||
verses.word_meanings: avyaktaḥ—unmanifest; akṣaraḥ—imperishable; iti uktaḥ—thus described; tam—that; āhuḥ—they declare; paramām gatim—the supreme destination; yam prāpya—reaching which; na nivartante—they never return; tat—that; dhāma paramam—supreme abode; mama—My.
verses.translation: That which is described as the Unmanifest and Imperishable is called the Supreme Goal. Those who reach it never return; that is My supreme abode.
verses.meaning: The highest spiritual state is known as Akshara (Imperishable) and Avyakta (Unmanifest to physical senses). This eternal divine realm (Dhama) of Sri Krishna is the supreme sanctuary of peace and immortality, reaching which the liberated soul never returns to material transmigration.
verses.purport: The highest spiritual state is known as Akshara (Imperishable) and Avyakta (Unmanifest to physical senses). This eternal divine realm (Dhama) of Sri Krishna is the supreme sanctuary of peace and immortality, reaching which the liberated soul never returns to material transmigration.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया |
यस्यान्तःस्थानि भूतानि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् || २२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया |
यस्यान्तःस्थानि भूतानि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् || २२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
puruṣaḥ sa paraḥ pārtha bhaktyā labhyastvananyayā |
yasyāntaḥsthāni bhūtāni yena sarvamidaṃ tatam || 22 ||
verses.word_meanings: puruṣaḥ saḥ paraḥ—that Supreme Person; pārtha—O son of Pritha; bhaktyā—by devotion; labhyaḥ—attainable; tu—indeed; ananyayā—by unalloyed, exclusive; yasya antaḥ-sthāni—within whom dwell; bhūtāni—all living entities; yena—by whom; sarvam idam—all this universe; tatam—is pervaded.
verses.translation: That Supreme Person, O Partha, in whom all beings reside and by whom all this universe is pervaded, is attainable solely by unalloyed and unwavering devotion (Ananya Bhakti).
verses.meaning: The Supreme Purusha is all-pervading and sustains the entire matrix of cosmic existence within His being. Despite His infinite transcendence, He is readily reachable through single-minded, pure, loving devotion (Bhaktya labhyas tv ananyaya), underscoring Bhakti as the crowning bridge between human consciousness and the Divine.
verses.purport: The Supreme Purusha is all-pervading and sustains the entire matrix of cosmic existence within His being. Despite His infinite transcendence, He is readily reachable through single-minded, pure, loving devotion (Bhaktya labhyas tv ananyaya), underscoring Bhakti as the crowning bridge between human consciousness and the Divine.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यत्र काले त्वनावृत्तिमावृत्तिं चैव योगिनः |
प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि भरतर्षभ || २३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यत्र काले त्वनावृत्तिमावृत्तिं चैव योगिनः |
प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि भरतर्षभ || २३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yatra kāle tvanāvṛttimāvṛttiṃ caiva yoginaḥ |
prayātā yānti taṃ kālaṃ vakṣyāmi bharatarṣabha || 23 ||
verses.word_meanings: yatra kāle—at which time/path; tu—indeed; anāvṛttim—no return (liberation); āvṛttim ca eva—and return (rebirth); yoginaḥ—yogis; prayātāḥ—departing; yānti—attain; tam kālam—that time/path; vakṣyāmi—I shall describe; bharatarṣabha—O best of the Bharatas (Arjuna).
verses.translation: I shall now declare unto you, O best of the Bharatas, the times (and paths) departing at which yogis attain liberation without return, or return again to mortal rebirth.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna prepares to explain the classical Upanishadic doctrine (found in Chandogya Upanishad 5.10) of the two cosmic paths of departure from this world: the path of no return (Anavritti / Devayana) and the path of rebirth (Avritti / Pitriyana).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अग्निर्ज्योतिरहः शुक्लः षण्मासा उत्तरायणम् |
तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः || २४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अग्निर्ज्योतिरहः शुक्लः षण्मासा उत्तरायणम् |
तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः || २४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
agnirjyotirahaḥ śuklaḥ ṣaṇmāsā uttarāyaṇam |
tatra prayātā gacchanti brahma brahmavido janāḥ || 24 ||
verses.word_meanings: agniḥ—fire; jyotiḥ—light; ahaḥ—day; śuklaḥ—the bright fortnight (waxing moon); ṣaṇ-māsāḥ uttarāyaṇam—the six months of the northern solstice; tatra—there; prayātāḥ—departed souls; gacchanti—reach; brahma—Brahman; brahma-vidaḥ janāḥ—people who know Brahman.
verses.translation: Fire, light, daytime, the bright fortnight of the waxing moon, and the six months of the northern solar course (Uttarayana)—departing along this illuminated path, knowers of Brahman attain Brahman.
verses.meaning: The luminous path of the gods (Devayana or Shukla Gati): These terms symbolize levels of illumination and spiritual awakening, presided over by luminous deities of light, day, the waxing moon, and the northward passage of the sun. Those illuminated with Self-knowledge who depart under these conditions attain supreme liberation without returning to samsara.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
धूमो रात्रिस्तथा कृष्णः षण्मासा दक्षिणायनम् |
तत्र चान्द्रमसं ज्योतिर्योगी प्राप्य निवर्तते || २५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
धूमो रात्रिस्तथा कृष्णः षण्मासा दक्षिणायनम् |
तत्र चान्द्रमसं ज्योतिर्योगी प्राप्य निवर्तते || २५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
dhūmo rātristathā kṛṣṇaḥ ṣaṇmāsā dakṣiṇāyanam |
tatra cāndramasaṃ jyotiryogī prāpya nivartate || 25 ||
verses.word_meanings: dhūmaḥ—smoke; rātriḥ—night; tathā—as well as; kṛṣṇaḥ—the dark fortnight (waning moon); ṣaṇ-māsāḥ dakṣiṇāyanam—the six months of the southern solstice; tatra—there; cāndramasam jyotiḥ—the lunar light/sphere; yogī—the practitioner; prāpya—having reached; nivartate—returns.
verses.translation: Smoke, night, the dark fortnight of the waning moon, and the six months of the southern solar course (Dakshinayana)—departing along this path, the yogi reaches the lunar sphere and returns again.
verses.meaning: The path of the ancestors (Pitriyana or Krishna Gati): Symbolized by smoke, darkness, and the southern solstice, this represents the trajectory of seekers motivated by ritualistic karma and temporary heavenly desires. Upon exhausting their celestial merits in the lunar sphere (Chandramasam Jyoti), they return once more to the mortal realm.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते |
एकया यात्यनावृत्तिमन्ययाऽऽवर्तते पुनः || २६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते |
एकया यात्यनावृत्तिमन्ययाऽऽवर्तते पुनः || २६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
śuklakṛṣṇe gatī hyete jagataḥ śāśvate mate |
ekayā yātyanāvṛttimanyayā''vartate punaḥ || 26 ||
verses.word_meanings: śukla-kṛṣṇe—the bright and the dark; gatī—two paths; hi—verily; ete—these; jagataḥ—of the world; śāśvate—eternal; mate—are considered; ekayā—by the one; yāti—goes to; anāvṛttim—non-return (liberation); anyayā—by the other; āvartate punaḥ—returns again.
verses.translation: These two paths of the world—the bright path (Shukla) and the dark path (Krishna)—are considered eternal. By the one, a person goes to liberation without return; by the other, one returns again to mortal life.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna summarizes the eternal cosmic paths. The bright path of wisdom and divine surrender leads to complete liberation (Anavritti), whereas the dark path of egoic desire and ritualism leads back to the cycles of birth and death (Avartate punah).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
नैते सृती पार्थ जानन्योगी मुह्यति कश्चन |
तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु योगयुक्तो भवार्जुन || २७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
नैते सृती पार्थ जानन्योगी मुह्यति कश्चन |
तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु योगयुक्तो भवार्जुन || २७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
naite sṛtī pārtha jānanyogī muhyati kaścana |
tasmātsarveṣu kāleṣu yogayukto bhavārjuna || 27 ||
verses.word_meanings: na—not; ete—these; sṛtī—two paths; pārtha—O son of Pritha; jānan—knowing; yogī—a yogi; muhyati—is deluded; kaścana—any; tasmāt—therefore; sarveṣu kāleṣu—at all times; yoga-yuktaḥ bhava—be established in yoga; arjuna—O Arjuna.
verses.translation: Knowing these two paths, O Partha, no yogi is ever deluded. Therefore, at all times, O Arjuna, remain steadfastly united in yoga.
verses.meaning: Understanding the profound truth of these two trajectories eliminates fear and confusion. The yogi does not worry about the external calendar or astronomical conditions at death, but focuses instead on perpetual inner union with God at every moment ('Tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu yogayukto bhavārjuna').

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
वेदेषु यज्ञेषु तपःसु चैव
दानेषु यत्पुण्यफलं प्रदिष्टम् |
अत्येति तत्सर्वमिदं विदित्वा
योगी परं स्थानमुपैति चाद्यम् || २८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
वेदेषु यज्ञेषु तपःसु चैव
दानेषु यत्पुण्यफलं प्रदिष्टम् |
अत्येति तत्सर्वमिदं विदित्वा
योगी परं स्थानमुपैति चाद्यम् || २८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
vedeṣu yajñeṣu tapaḥsu caiva
dāneṣu yatpuṇyaphalaṃ pradiṣṭam |
atyeti tatsarvamidaṃ viditvā
yogī paraṃ sthānamupaiti cādyam || 28 ||
verses.word_meanings: vedeṣu—in the study of the Vedas; yajñeṣu—in the performance of sacrifices; tapaḥsu—in austerities; ca eva—and also; dāneṣu—in giving charities; yat—which; puṇya-phalam—fruit of merit; pradiṣṭam—ordained; atyeti—transcends; tat sarvam—all that; idam viditvā—knowing this; yogī—the yogi; param sthānam—the Supreme Abode; upaiti—attains; ca—and; ādyam—the primeval, original.
verses.translation: Whatever meritorious fruit is declared for Vedic study, sacrifices, austerities, and charities—the yogi, knowing this profound truth, transcends them all and reaches the Supreme, Primeval Abode.
verses.meaning: The concluding verse of Chapter 8 summarizes the unparalleled supremacy of Self-knowledge and devotion. Conventional pious acts—Vedic chanting, fire sacrifices (Yajna), rigorous penances (Tapas), and philanthropic charity (Dana)—yield rewarding but finite fruits. The enlightened yogi who masters the teachings of Akshara Brahma Yoga surpasses all worldly and heavenly rewards, ascending directly to the supreme, beginningless sanctuary of the Absolute (Param Sthanam Adyam).
